summary: Milestone 2026.08.536 completed 12 experiments in 30.8 minutes, including 4 compute-bound experiments. The longest listed compute-bound work was the 5.82-minute live dual-family strategy seed stream, followed by the 0.69-minute authentic Gemma code pool; both descriptions identify an Exp6186 bank-readiness gate, but the supplied data does not isolate why their durations differed. The locked task-conditioned GPU-idle classification is false, while the snapshot is not linked to an experiment interval and supplies no evidence of a parallel multi-model DualGPURunner miss.
bottlenecks_identified: The 13.0-minute reliable dated-evidence refresh was the longest listed experiment and was synthesis-only, making evidence-refresh latency the clearest elapsed-time concentration without implicating GPU use.

The 10.67-minute Rust/PyO3 sampler correctness and distribution-parity task was the next-longest listed experiment and was also synthesis-only, indicating a second non-GPU execution path worth instrumenting.

The compute-bound entries name an Exp6186 bank-readiness gate, but no phase-level timing separates dependency wait, model startup, generation, and validation, so the cause of the 5.82-minute compute-bound duration cannot be determined from the supplied data.
The locked compute-task classification reports no GPU-idle condition. The idle GPU snapshot is not task-correlated evidence and therefore is not identified as a milestone bottleneck.
No supplied timing or GPU record establishes that a task loaded multiple models in parallel, so no missed DualGPURunner engagement can be identified.
improvements_suggested: Add content-addressed incremental receipts to the dated-evidence refresh so unchanged inputs can bypass repeated synthesis work.
Add phase timers to Rust/PyO3 parity work so build, binding, correctness, and distribution checks can be optimized independently.
Emit a bank-readiness receipt before admitting dependent compute work, and record dependency-wait time separately from execution time.
Persist task-scoped GPU intervals with workload identity, model count, and runner selection; require DualGPURunner only when at least two models are actually loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Make the dated-evidence refresh incremental with content-addressed reuse.
Instrument synthesis and compute phases, including explicit Exp6186 readiness-wait accounting.
Record task-correlated GPU, model-count, and runner-selection receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner routing for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The bounded timing list supports runtime ranking but not causal attribution, and the GPU snapshot is not linked to an active experiment interval. Estimated savings therefore remain 0 rather than assigning an unmeasured speedup to the proposed tooling.
